title: Polymarket bot — fidelity (paper)
description: WP-240 fidelity view: how trustworthy the data and the simulation are. The dataset and staleness half is bound to WP-140's recorder exporter, which is a real producer running today. The replay/determinism and simulation-fidelity half has NO producer in this repository, and each such panel says so, names what would produce it, and names the owner — rather than binding to an invented metric that would read blank forever.

panels.title: Dataset validation
panels.description: §12.5 dataset manifests. recorder_validation_ok is 0 when the last validation run found anything; recorder_validation_findings counts them. A replay run against a dataset whose validation is not clean is a replay whose result means less than it looks.

panels.title: Feed staleness and gaps
panels.description: §14.3 feed: staleness by source, resyncs, data-quality incidents. Every series here is a reason a downstream feature, decision or fill is less trustworthy than it appears.

panels.title: Recorder WAL data-loss bound
panels.description: The recorder's own honesty metric: the maximum window of frames that are accepted but not yet proven durable. A replay of a window in which this was large is a replay over data that might be incomplete.

panels.title: Compaction lag
panels.description: How far Parquet/manifest production trails the WAL. A large lag means the dataset a replay would read does not yet include recent live behaviour.

panels.title: Replay determinism
panels.description: This panel is intentionally not bound to a metric. See its content.

options.content:
PENDING PRODUCER: a determinism indicator emitted by whatever executes a replay; §12.4 determinism is proven today by `pnpm test:replay` and test/replay-golden, which emit no metric at all — OWNER: a future packages/simulation or apps/backtest-cli grant (WP-250 verifies determinism but its allowed paths forbid packages/** and apps/**, so it cannot add a producer)

Until then, determinism evidence is a GATE, not a dashboard: `pnpm test:replay` must pass and the golden output must be byte-identical across runs. Do not read the absence of a red panel here as evidence that a replay was deterministic.

panels.title: Predicted versus actual fills
panels.description: This panel is intentionally not bound to a metric. See its content.

options.content:
PENDING PRODUCER: §12.2's execution-calibration model, which compares simulated fills against observed ones. It requires EXECUTION_PROBE data that does not and may not exist under MAX_RUN_MODE=PAPER — OWNER: WP-290 / phase-4 execution probes (out of scope for phase 2 by the phase plan)

The simulated venue currently runs the Tier 0 pipeline smoke model. Its fills are a property of the model, not a prediction to score, so a 'predicted versus actual' chart drawn from them would compare the model with itself.

panels.title: Markout
panels.description: This panel is intentionally not bound to a metric. See its content.

options.content:
PENDING PRODUCER: §12.3 markout computation over fills; packages/simulation computes markouts for research output, and nothing exports them as a time series — OWNER: a future packages/simulation or apps/research-worker grant

When it lands, note that a markout is an exact decimal: it belongs on this surface as an `_info` label carrying the decimal string, not as a float64 gauge (§6 invariant 1).
